title: Proposal to Defer GST Increase Given Increased Tax Collection in FY2021/2022 and Below-inflation Income Growth
what_it_is: Proposal to Defer GST Increase Given Increased Tax Collection in FY2021/2022 and Below-inflation Income Growth

sections.label: Wage support and tax revenue
sections.summary: Government will spend about $9 billion on transitional wage support and Workfare, while stamp duty drove FY2021 revenue increase, which cannot be relied on as stable revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And as announced at Budget this year, the Government will also spend about $9 billion on transitional wage support to businesses and Workfare enhancements, as part of our commitment to help workers achieve broad-based and sustainable income growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We experienced revenue increase of more than 22% in FY2021 and this sharp increase is partly due to a lower tax base in FY2020 arising from the impact of the pandemic that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In particular, stamp duty collection accounted for the largest share of the tax revenue increase in FY2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But just as a bullish property market can provide upsides, there can also be downsides in a muted market, as past experience has shown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We therefore cannot rely on such sentiment-driven collections, which can fluctuate from year to year, as a stable and sustainable source of revenue to meet our rising recurrent expenditure needs.

sections.label: GST increase and household impact
sections.summary: Measures including the GST increase will proceed as planned, with most Singaporean households unaffected for at least five years and lower-income households for about 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: These will provide us with the resources we need to meet our longer-term priorities in a responsible manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will proceed with these measures, including the GST increase as planned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But as I have assured Members previously, we will also ensure that the majority of Singaporean households will not feel the impact of the GST increase for at least five years, while lower-income households will not feel the impact for about 10 years.

sections.label: Projecting tax revenue better
sections.summary: A question asks how the Ministry will better project and estimate tax revenue following the higher than expected $60.7 billion collected in FY2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In light of the higher than expected $60.7 billion tax revenue collected in FY2021, how will the Ministry better project and estimate tax revenue in the future, so that we can better fine-tune our fiscal and monetary strategies so that we can better implement measures pertaining to tax policies?

sections.label: Whether deficits will materialise
sections.summary: A question asks Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong whether the expected $5 billion FY2021 deficit and $3 billion FY2022 deficit will materialise given strong revenue growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: My question, Speaker, to Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong is: bottom line, whether the expected overall deficit of $5 billion in FY2021 and the deficit of $3 billion in FY2022 will actually materialise in light of the strong revenue growth.

sections.label: Balanced budget and income growth
sections.summary: The aim is a balanced budget over the medium term, with readiness to do more if the economy worsens, and comparison of income growth with higher inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our aim is not to accumulate a surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our aim is to run a balanced budget over the medium term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At the same time, if the economic situation worsens, as we have said, we will be prepared to do more to support and help Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are looking at Singaporeans' income growth across all the different segments and comparing with the higher inflation that they are experiencing to see where the gap is, after taking into consideration the transfers and help measures that we have provided.
